introduction.text: The Church of Santissima Trinità dei Monti, commonly known as Trinità dei Monti, is a Roman Catholic church in Rome situated above the Spanish Steps. Its historical and artistic significance, along with its role as a French national church, make it a notable landmark in the city.

history.description: In 1494, King Charles VIII of France purchased part of the ancient Gardens of Lucullus and secured papal permission to establish a monastery for the Minim Order.
In 1502, Louis XII began construction of the church of Trinità dei Monti to celebrate his successful invasion of the Kingdom of Naples.
The present Italian Renaissance church was consecrated in 1585 by Pope Sixtus V.
In 1587, the Titulus Santissimae Trinitatis in Monte Pincio was established, making the church a titular church.
In 1789, the Obelisco Sallustiano was moved to the front of the church.
During the French Revolution, the church suffered partial destruction in 1798.
In 1816, the church was restored at the expense of King Louis XVIII after the Bourbon restoration.
In 1828, the complex was entrusted to the Religious of the Sacred Heart.
In 2006, the school closed and the complex was transferred to the Monastic Fraternities of Jerusalem.
In 2016, the care of the complex was transferred to the Emmanuel Community.

design.description: The church was originally begun in a French Gothic style but was ultimately completed in the Italian Renaissance style, featuring a prominent façade possibly designed by Giacomo della Porta and a double staircase by Domenico Fontana.

art.description: The interior houses works by notable artists such as Giambattista Naldini, Daniele da Volterra, Cesare Nebbia, Perino del Vaga, and others, including frescoes and canvases depicting biblical scenes.
